title: Phononic raises $100m debt facility to fund solid-state cooling system
html:
Solid-state cooling vendor Phononic has raised $100 million in debt financing to scale up its manufacturing capability.

Trinity Capital will provide the debt facility, which will be used to “support accelerated growth and manufacturing capacity expansion to meet increasing customer demand.”

Based in North Carolina, Phononic is marketing a thermoelectric cooling solution, which works by using an electric current to stimulate a temperature change in a special class of semiconductor materials known as calorics. These materials are able to absorb heat from IT hardware and cool down rapidly, expelling the heat elsewhere.

While this kind of system enables cooling without a lot of the moving parts and cooling fluids required in more established methods, the technology is not yet efficient enough to cool an entire data center.

Phononic appears to be targeting specific parts of the server for its cooling system, providing supplementary cooling products that can sit directly on components such as lasers and memory chips. This should, in theory, increase the performance of these components and take pressure off the main data center cooling system.

"AI infrastructure is advancing at an unprecedented pace, and cooling has become a critical bottleneck to growth, limiting both facility capacity and compute and optical performance. Our customers are demanding disruptive thermal control solutions that can overcome these limitations at scale," said Dr. Tony Atti, CEO and founder of Phononic.

"Our partnership with Trinity Capital enables us to accelerate manufacturing capacity expansion to meet that demand and support the next wave of growth across AI infrastructure."

Phononic also offers a software system to manage its cooling hardware.

"As AI hardware continues to evolve, we believe precise, real-time cooling at the chip level is becoming increasingly important," said Phil Gager, senior managing director of tech lending at Trinity Capital. "Phononic has built the thermoelectric technology and software to address that need, and we're pleased to back their team as demand for their solutions continues to build."

DCD took an in-depth look at solid-state cooling systems in our latest Cooling Supplement, out now.
summary: Will provide cooling at chip level
